title: Chandra Pal Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Abhinava Upadhya, J.; Shamim Ahmed, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioners relegated to CGRF under Clause 7.10.
headnote: Electricity-bill writ disposed following Ram Autar: consumers directed to the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under Clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; delay alone is not a ground to reject the application.
facts: Chandra Pal Singh and others filed Writ-C No. 23377 of 2012 against U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. over disputed electricity bills. On 14 May 2012 a Division Bench connected the petition with Writ-C No. 11961 of 2012, stayed recovery of the impugned bill if rural-area minimum fixed charges were deposited each month, and allowed meter installation, leaving metered versus lump-sum liability to the result of the writ. The petition remained pending until 26 February 2020.

holding_units.holding: On a dispute of electricity bill, the Court followed Ram Autar and disposed of the writ by directing the petitioners to appear before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum created under Clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, making clear that if they approach the Forum their application will not be thrown out only on account of delay.

not_decided.point: Whether the petitioners are liable to pay metered charges or lump-sum fixed charges, and the correctness of the impugned bill
not_decided.note: The 2012 interim order reserved that question to the result of the writ; the 2020 disposal sent the billing controversy to the CGRF without deciding it.

authorities.name: Ram Autar v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
